newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says many critical of bank role in merger.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says many critical of bank role in merger.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday that Germany's banks should exercise more self-control so as not to fan public fears over unbridled power of the nation's financial institutions.

Commenting on the role of two leading banks in a hostile takeover bid for industry group Thyssen AG by Krupp, Rexrodt said in a statement the banks should "direct their own actions so as not to feed this discussion about misuse of power".
"The role of the banks in the takeover attempt of Thyssen by its competitor Krupp left a bitter aftertaste for many people," Rexrodt said.
Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp had the backing of Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank -- Germany's two largest banks -- and U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs for its takeover bid.

Deutsche Bank chairman Hilmar Kopper at the bank's annual results news conference on Wednesday dismissed criticism of the bank's support for the takeover bid and said he did not believe the bank would be hurt by its involvement.
"We dont think our image has been damaged, seen professionally," he said. "On the contrary."

Rexrodt dismissed criticism from the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) that the federal government was delaying plans to introduce legislation that would curb the power that banks may wield over industry.
"The government in its draft legislation for control and transparency in industry and will establish a series of measures to counter the abuse of power by the banks," Rexrodt said.
The draft bill, that has not yet been presented to parliament, however, would not have been able to block Krupp's unsolicited takeover bid for Thyssen, he added.
The SPD has urged the government to limit the number of board seats bankers may have in companies as well as restrict the voting powers of banks at shareholders meetings.
Rexrodt said he welcomed the fact that Krupp and Thyssen appear close to agreeing on merging their steel companies and that there would be no compulsory redundancies as a result.
"The competitiveness of the German steel industry will be increased through the merger of their steel activities," he said. "The path they have taken is also in the interest of workers."
